Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model, reviewed_by null); no hardware run and no human review is claimed. The upstream clone was not imported or run; dartpy is not installed, so the fake backend is this package's pure-Python stand-in (fake.py: a damped pendulum plus the cart velocity the action sets) and it was not compared with the upstream environment. The sim backend (gymnasium.make('DartCartPole-v0')) was not run: as committed the upstream step() returns the legacy 3-tuple (gym_dart/envs/dart_cartpole_env.py:74-80) and reset() takes no seed (:70-72), which the gymnasium bridge cannot serve; the fidelity gaps record this. The upstream world timestep is 10 ms (:36), the action space is Box(-5, 5) (:59-66) and the 200-step registration limit is gym_dart/__init__.py:12. No Limit is declared because the only bound is the action space the bridge derives; the device is simulated R0. Expected warnings, left unchanged: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only sets the seed of the next reset, so it makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the integer/number inputs the bridge derives (ticks, action.values[*], seed on reset, seed on the seed class). Only catalogue classes (cap.world.reset/step/seed) are used, so there are no catalogue requests. NOT COVERED: the upstream environment on the sim backend, rendering, snapshot/restore, and agreement between the fake and DART. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed.
